Description: Add generators with very high marginal cost to simulate load shedding and avoid problem infeasibilities. If load shedding is a float, it denotes the marginal cost in $/kWh.
To avoid too small values in the renewables` per-unit availability time series values below this threshold are set to zero.
Add random noise to marginal cost of generators by :math:`\mathcal{U}(0.009,0,011)` and capital cost of lines and links by :math:`\mathcal{U}(0.09,0,11)`.
Skip iterating, do not update impedances of branches. Defaults to true.
Whether to optimize the network in a rolling horizon manner, where the snapshot range is split into slices of size horizon which are solved consecutively.
Random seed for increased deterministic behaviour.
Flag whether to store the intermediate branch capacities and objective function values are recorded for each iteration in ``network.lines['s_nom_opt_X']`` (where ``X`` labels the iteration)

Defaults to ``slp``. How the capacity dependence of line impedance (and of the SSSC term) is resolved when ``skip_iterations`` is false. ``fp``: fixed point, impedances are frozen at the previous iteration's capacities. ``slp``: sequential linear programming, the voltage law carries the first-order sensitivity to the line capacity, and an adaptive quadratic proximal term damps the step. This makes every iteration a QP, so use Gurobi; HiGHS' QP solver can stall.

Convergence criterion on the step of the extendable line capacities: RMS of the change from the capacities the impedances were taken at, relative to their mean. The iteration stops once both this and ``cost_threshold`` are met.
Convergence criterion on the relative change of the system cost (without the proximal term) from the previous iteration.
Maximum number of solving iterations in between which resistance and reactence (``x/r``) are updated for branches according to ``s_nom_opt`` of the previous run.
Optional, ``slp`` only. Initial weight of the proximal term, in units of a line's capital cost per its own size. 0 switches the term off, so every iteration is an LP. Defaults to 0.5.
Optional, ``slp`` only. Double the proximal weight, up to ``proximal_ceiling``, when successive steps move capacity back. Defaults to true.
Optional, ``slp`` only. Upper bound of the adaptive proximal weight. Defaults to 4.
Optional, ``slp`` only. Line sensitivities below this share of the line's voltage drop at its capacity are dropped. Defaults to 1e-4.
Add piecewise linear approximation of transmission losses based on n tangents. 0 means losses are ignored; the shipped default is 2.
Whether to optimise using the linearized unit commitment formulation.
Number of snapshots in each rolling-horizon window (only used when ``rolling_horizon`` is true).
Whether to populate dual values (shadow prices) for every constraint after solving, not just the standard subset. Needed for downstream price and policy-cost reporting.
Solver to use for optimisation problems in the workflow; e.g. clustering and linear optimal power flow.
Name of solver_options to use from dictionary below.
Named blocks of solver-native tuning options (e.g. ``gurobi-default``, ``highs-default``); the block selected by ``solver: options`` is passed verbatim to the solver.
Wall-time cap for the solver itself. Per-rule scheduler walltimes are set separately in the top-level ``walltime:`` section.
